articles.title: ‘I wanted to create the female version of a man’s suit’: how Roland Mouret’s Galaxy dress took over the world
articles.summary: One the most famous dresses of this century, it was worn by royalty and A-list celebrities in the noughties. Its latest fans are Maga women. Here, the designer, and former mentor to Victoria Beckham, reveals the story behind it.
body: The story of one of the most photographed and ripped-off dresses of the last 50 years came together with a simple zip. It was 1998; the designer Roland Mouret had shown his first collection at London fashion week and was looking for a way to produce good clothes at speed. He connected with a small British atelier and it was there that some old-school industry wisdom would alter his course: he learned that a longer seam doesn’t actually cost any more than a shorter one.

Despite his brilliantly instinctive approach to design, it was like cracking a code – and steered him towards the dress that would make his name. “My brain was buzzing!” he says. “I hadn’t thought about it before – if you extend a top by 50cm, it becomes a whole outfit. You just need accessories. Focusing on dresses gives you a signature piece at the right price.”
points: One the most famous dresses of this century, it was worn by royalty and A-list celebrities in the noughties.

articles.title: 18 again: I returned to my life in 1983 – to reckless adventures, in a world soaked in alcohol
articles.summary: Sundays were deadly, the generation gap between parents and their kids was enormous, and a pint cost 50p. The frisson of casual violence was everywhere. When I left school and set off to travel, I had no sense at all of where I was going or what I would find.
body: I am wandering down a steep and unfamiliar street in Saint Peter Port, Guernsey, a force seven gale blowing in my face, when I look up to cross the road and see a back garden running up the hillside opposite. It ends in a granite rock face about 30ft high, and in that moment, I have a vivid flashback to being sat on top of it, watching a group of people in the garden below. I can’t conjure their faces, but the memory is all too real: the sun on my face, a woman calling up: “Don’t break your neck!” I can tell she’s not worried and neither am I. Nobody is. It’s a party and we’re young and we’re drunk and we’re carefree, without a worry in the world. Or at least, that’s how I remember it.
There are no lights on, no car outside. I carry on down to the coast, where huge waves crash against the sea wall.

articles.title: You be the judge: should my husband stop letting our cat drink on the kitchen counter?
articles.summary: James says Tony leaving the cat’s water bowl where they prepare food is unhygienic. Should they feed their feline on the floor? You decide. • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. It’s unhygienic.
body: I’ve been married to Tony for 10 years. We understand each other’s quirks, but he is a very intense person with many passions, and one of his passions is cats.
We have three cats, adopted from Brazil. Growing up, I was a dog person, but I also used to rescue stray cats, so I love them too. But Tony is obsessed.

We also had a dog, Jamie, but he died recently. He developed a digestive problem, aged 14, because he over-ate. He often ate the cats’ food, so we moved the cats’ bowls up on to the counter next to the kitchen sink to stop this. One cat, Juçara, got particularly used to eating and drinking up there.

Now the dog isn’t around, but Tony will still leave the water bowl on the kitchen counter. I find it unhygienic. Juçara will jump straight out of her litter box and on to the surface where we prepare food. It’s too much.
points: James says Tony leaving the cat’s water bowl where they prepare food is unhygienic.

articles.title: Chinese Design Is Booming. What Does That Mean for Western Luxury?
articles.summary: As global luxury brands see demand shrink in China, emerging domestic designers are maturing. Can they turn recognition into lasting businesses?
body: Until recently, China’s importance to the global fashion industry has been largely measured by consumption: its appetite for luxury rather than its ability to produce the next generation of talent.

Now, against a backdrop of economic uncertainty, China’s luxury market is recalibrating, says Fflur Roberts, head of luxury goods at Euromonitor International. “Weaker consumer confidence, slower economic growth and heightened price sensitivity are weighing on discretionary spending, following more than a decade in which China was a key driver of global luxury growth,” she says.

And although China’s personal luxury goods market showed signs of stabilization in 2025, luxury fashion remained under pressure, and according to figures from Euromonitor, is still down considerably from its peak in 2023 (approximately $460 million, versus a projected $407 million for 2027). LVMH earlier this month posted a 5% drop in sales for the third quarter for fashion and leather goods, laying the blame on “less buoyant demand” in China. For global brands to maintain relevance in this environment, Roberts adds, it will require more than longstanding prestige.
points: As global luxury brands see demand shrink in China, emerging domestic designers are maturing.

articles.title: The 2026 CFDA Nominees and Honorees Are In—Anthony Vaccarello Named International Designer of the Year
articles.summary: From Ralph Lauren to Carolina Herrera and Public School New York, this year’s CFDA nominees represent an exciting lineup of American fashion legacies.
body: Ahead of the Council of Fashion Designers of America cocktail party tonight, followed by six full days of spring 2027 shows here in New York City—seven if you count Rachel Comey, Ralph Lauren, and Coach later today—the organization has announced its 2026 nominees and honorees. All will be celebrated at the CFDA Fashion Awards, presented by Amazon Fashion and hosted by Keke Palmer, on November 2.

Carolina Herrera’s Wes Gordon, who is celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary this season, is nominated for a second consecutive year for American womenswear designer of the year. He joins a roster that includes two-time winner Catherine Holstein for Khaite, former winner Michael Kors, two-time nominee Tory Burch, and Diotima’s Rachel Scott, who won in 2024—a full lineup spanning generations of American fashion.

articles.title: Hermès Sales Rise 4.3% in Q3
articles.summary: This marks a deceleration compared with the last quarter, when sales were up more than 6%.
body: Hermès reported sales were up 4.3% at constant exchange rates to €4 billion in the third quarter of 2026, below expectations of 5.2%. This marks a deceleration from Q2, when Hermès’s sales were up 6.7%.

“Despite a complex environment, Hermès continues its profitable growth and maintains its course,” Hermès executive chair Axel Dumas said in a statement. “Convinced of the strength and relevance of our artisanal model, we see our vision as firmly rooted in the long term, and we look to the future with confidence.”

Dumas continued: “It is with great enthusiasm that we prepare for a new year rich in creation, with the first men’s ready-to-wear collection signed by Grace Wales Bonner and the introduction of couture by Nadège Vanhée next January.”
In the third quarter, growth was led by the Americas (up 8.8%), Japan (up 9.6 %) and Europe (up 7.2%). Asia-Pacific, excluding Japan, was flat. Other regions including the Middle East were down 4.5%.

articles.title: The Eggs Scene in ‘You Can See Everything’ Scrambles Reality
articles.summary: This review contains spoilers for the film You Can See Everything. A version of this post originally appeared in Eater Today, which spotlights the freshest news and stories from across the food world every day. Subscribe now.
body: What happens when you take two unreliable narrators — make that three, if you include Holmes’s partner, Billy Evans, whose on-camera persona morphs from protective, naive tech bro to unscrupulous grifter — put them in a jar, and shake them? The result is that the more questions are asked, the further the truth drifts out of reach. It’s like staring at a Magic Eye image, slightly crossing your eyes, desperate to make out the hidden 3D subject but never quite managing to see it. Eventually, you start worrying your eyes might get stuck that way.
The discourse surrounding the film is already abundant, but we’re here to talk about the eggs.

If you’re familiar with the hallmarks of Fielderian programming, you know that Fielder is prone to hyperfixating on seemingly mundane details that later return to completely upend viewers’ expectations. In You Can See Everything, one such detail is observed in an exchange between Holmes and Evans as they make eggs. How much can be gleaned from watching someone make breakfast? A lot, apparently.

articles.title: Teen Vogue and Wattpad Launched Their New Romance Series with Tarot Readings and Zodiac-Inspired Looks
articles.summary: Teen Vogue hosted an astrology-themed bash at downtown bookstore McNally Jackson to celebrate the launch of I Saw The Signs, its original romance fiction series in partnership with Wattpad Books.
body: Earlier that day, the inaugural installment had dropped. The first chapter of the book Under The Northern Stars by Tay Marley is described by Teen Vogue’s creative editorial director Mi-Anne Chan as “a spicy romance between a science-obsessed nerdy girl and her boy-next-door, teen bronco-riding champion neighbor.” The other books, Read To Me by Ariana Godoy and ​​Star-Crossed Rivals by Anna Todd and E.M. Wilson, will debut in early 2027, each using astrology as a lens to explore relationships.

The original fiction project is the first of its kind for Teen Vogue and a “natural next step” according to Chan, given the publication’s past coverage of fanbases within youth culture. Fan fiction also provides a “world building” opportunity and a chance to invite audiences to find their niche. This is part of Wattpad’s draw for young creatives, too—its self-publishing and community format encourages judgment-free expression and imagination. “You can explore a lot of different themes through a familiar world and familiar stories. It’s the way that writers develop their voice, in the way that they explore things through different universes,” Chan explained.

articles.title: The United States Just Got a New National Park For the First Time in Six Years
articles.summary: Located in the southeastern corner of Arizona, this 12,000-acre park is known for its unique rock formations, pristine stargazing, and scenic canyon drives.
body: The US national park list is growing for the first time in nearly six years. Chiricahua National Monument, located in southeastern Arizona, was officially designated as the 64th national park in the US on October 20, 2026 following President Trump's signature on the Chiricahua National Park Act.

The new park lies just over an hour from the Arizona–New Mexico border and is nicknamed the “Wonderland of Rocks” for its towering rock spires and unusual formations, the result of a volcanic eruption about 27 million years ago.

Chiricahua was originally established as a national monument in 1924, and today boasts more than 17 miles of hiking trails for exploring on foot, as well as the Bonita Canyon Scenic Drive, a picturesque road that winds through rock formations.

For outdoors lovers, the designation is big news. The last US landmark to receive a new national park designation was West Virginia’s New River Gorge National Park & Preserve in 2020, home to one of the oldest rivers in the world and the deepest and longest river gorge in the Appalachians.

articles.title: This Ultra-Wide Samsung Gaming Monitor Is $600 Off
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. Deal pricing and availability subject to change after time of publication. An ultra-wide curved gaming monitor with ridiculous specs is every gamer's dream, but they (usually) don't come cheap.
body: The Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 Series is not a regular ultra-wide gaming monitor. It has impressive specs, but you'll need a top-notch gaming computer with specific outputs to take full advantage of its 240Hz refresh rate potential.

This monitor came out in 2023 with an "excellent" review from PCMag, mainly due to its impressive 7,680 by 2,160 4K native resolution, the ridiculous 57-inch screen size, its great color range and accuracy, the 240Hz refresh rate, and its design. The VA panel also means you get a bright 1,000-nit screen. To make full use of its powerful 240Hz refresh rate, you'll need to use a DisplayPort 2.1, or you'll be limited to 120Hz. You'll also need a powerful modern graphics card that is able to push the frames at a native resolution to max out the monitor's potential.

Although it is pricey, this monitor is a great value for the right gamer. You'll need plenty of space to fit a 57-inch screen, as well as a powerful computer to justify using the monitor—if you're not a competitive gamer with a powerful computer, it's probably not worth the price tag. Instead, consider this Asus gaming monitor going for $329.99 (originally $499) right now.
